newsitem.title: CHINA: China extends grace period for HK right of abode.
newsitem.headline: China extends grace period for HK right of abode.

text.p: Beijing on Monday eased earlier rules, saying Hong Kong residents who want permanent right of abode in the territory no longer must be present in the British colony on the day it returns to Chinese sovereignty.

"While a person has the responsibility to assure immigration authorities that he is resident in Hong Kong on July 1, he does not have to be in Hong Kong in person on that day," the People's Daily quoted a spokesman for the cabinet's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office as saying.

China had previously said that Chinese wishing to establish permanent residency of the territory after it reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 should be present in Hong Kong on the day of the handover.
A Chinese resident could establish permanent right of abode in Hong Kong if he returned to the territory within 18 months of the handover, the newspaper quoted spokesman Wang Fengchao as saying.
Any Chinese will retain Hong Kong permanent residency status unless he or she lives outside the territory for a period exceeding 36 months before resettling in the territory, Wang said.
For non-Chinese permanent residents of Hong Kong, if they live outside the territory continuously for 36 months, they will forfeit their right of abode, Wang said.
He said six categories of people qualified for permanent residency of the territory that has been ruled by Britain for more than 150 years.

These include Chinese citizens born in Hong Kong before or after the handover and Chinese who have ordinarily resided in Hong Kong for a continuous period of not less than seven years before or after the handover.
Also included are Chinese born outside Hong Kong of those residents listed in the above categories.

Other categories are non-Chinese who have lived in Hong Kong for a continuous period of not less than seven years and have taken Hong Kong as their place of permanent residence, people under 21 and born in Hong Kong and people not among those listed above who had the right of abode in Hong Kong only.
